newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends up in cautious trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends up in cautious trading.

text.p: Shanghai B share index ended slightly up on Monday due to some institutional speculation in selected stocks, but most investors remained sidelined due to a lack of market-moving news, brokers said.
The B index rose 0.138 points or 0.21 percent to 65.707 on volume of 21.998 million shares worth $9.6 million.

"Institutional speculative buying of heavily-weighted stocks pushed the index up, but most investors took a wait-and-see attitude as Deng's death has been factored in and there is nothing else happening," said one broker.
"The market has entered a correction period after several days of rises," another broker said. "Listed companies' annual reports will be a key factor deciding its direction from here on."
Of 43 B shares, 42 traded with 18 up eight flat and 16 down.
Shanghai Diesel Engine was the star on a spurt of buying just ahead of the close, rising $0.016 or 3.20 percent to $0.516 on volume of 116,300 shares.
Market giant Shanghai Tyre and Rubber performed well on institutional support buying, gaining $0.012 or 2.62 percent to $0.470 on volume of 100,000 shares.

Textile machinery maker Shanghai Erfangji traded the most on overseas institutional selling despite domestic investors' speculative buying, ending down $0.002 or 1.12 percent to $0.176 on volume of 2.2 million shares.
Shanghai A shares closed down on profit-taking after sharp gains over the past few trading days, brokers said.
The index fell 8.198 points or 0.77 percent to 1055.078 points on volume of 1.0 billion shares worth 9.1 billion yuan.
The SSE30 index shed 15.799 points or 0.57 percent to 2751.238 points.
Yibin Paper was the biggest loser on profit-taking, falling 0.87 yuan or 6.47 percent to 12.57 yuan on volume of 2.6 million shares.
